card.summary: 1 active tunnel, 2 extra ports per tunnel, TCP and UDP support, Unlimited bandwidth

free_tier.stated: 1 active tunnel, 2 extra ports per tunnel, TCP and UDP support, Unlimited bandwidth

egress.terms: Unlimited bandwidth, stated for every plan: 'Every plan includes TCP, UDP, encrypted tunnels, and unlimited bandwidth.' No rate, meter or tolerated tolerance is published.; ingress: udp

record.interface_detail: pwrp login, pwrp tunnels, pwrp connect
record.chaining: one free UDP port is exactly one WireGuard endpoint: run wg-quick on the origin, point a free VM or a second tunnel at it, and the relay carries the datagrams

limits.value: no number published; 'unlimited bandwidth' is the whole of the stated allowance

record.binding_note: Free plan provides one active tunnel with unstated bandwidth limits. Dropped free tunnels require manual restart.

identity_cost.detail: a free account with browser device-code approval: 'Create an account in 30 seconds. No credit card.' https://portwarp.com/ ; 'The CLI opens a browser approval flow and displays a short code.' https://portwarp.com/docs/cli/quickstart

record.reliability_note: Auto-reconnect requires a PRO subscription; dropped free tunnels require manual client restart. Bandwidth rate limits are unpublished.
record.confidence_note: Raise to measured by running the CLI on a free account, holding a UDP port, reconnecting, and confirming the public port is unchanged after a restart; then pushing a counted byte volume through it for an hour and reading the transfer counter.

evidence.proved: free plan is 1 active tunnel with TCP and UDP support and unlimited bandwidth; PRO is USD 2.99/month with 32 tunnels
the tunnel's public port is listed as a stored property of the tunnel, not a per-session allocation; login is a browser device-code flow
'The CLI supports TCP, UDP, and tunnels that use both protocols. It only makes outbound connections'
'Native UDP & TCP Tunneling' and a LOCAL PORT 27015 to TUNNEL PORT 27015 mapping, plus 'No credit card'
portwarp.com:443 accepts a TCP connection from this host and the pricing page returns HTTP 200

record.notes: The strongest free-tier UDP candidate found that is not a game-preset tunnel: UDP is in the base plan, the port is configured rather than allocated, and the allowance is stated as unlimited. Not measured. The free tier's one-tunnel cap is a plan limit outside the constraint vocabulary and lives in binding_note. Re-read 2026-10-23: PRO adds 90-day traffic history and connection insights, so the edge counts bytes even though every plan is sold as unlimited.

extras.wg_detail: UDP is a native free-tier protocol and the public port is a property of the tunnel configured in the dashboard, not an allocation made at connect time: 'The list shows a number, name, protocol, local port, public port, and current state for each tunnel.' https://portwarp.com/docs/cli/quickstart
extras.volume_stated: Unlimited bandwidth, stated for every plan: 'Every plan includes TCP, UDP, encrypted tunnels, and unlimited bandwidth.' No rate, meter or tolerated tolerance is published.
extras.transit_note: the anycast edge carries the datagrams; the operator's POP is the single point of failure
